subject: Mathematical Literacy
standard: South African CAPS Mathematical Literacy -- FET Grades 10-12
prompt: Extract the full CAPS Mathematical Literacy syllabus for FET Grades 10-12 from the Department of Basic Education CAPS document. Return a structured JSON object with: (1) documentMeta -- subject='Mathematical Literacy', grade='10-12', phase='FET', sourcePdf, language='English', versionDate='January 2012', publisher; (2) contentAreas -- an array of 7 content areas, where the first two are Basic Skills Topics (Numbers and calculations with numbers, Patterns/relationships/representations) and the remaining five are Application Topics (Finance: 35% +/- 5%, Measurement: 20% +/- 5%, Maps/plans/representations of the physical world: 15% +/- 5%, Data handling: 25% +/- 5%, Probability: 5% to 10%). Each contentArea has contentArea name, type (Basic Skills Topic or Application Topic), weighting (for Application Topics the percentage; for Basic Skills Topics note 'no separate weighting -- assessed in an integrated way in Application Topics'), generalFocus (description of the real-world context focus), and topics -- each topic with topic name, subtopics (array of descriptors), and pacing -- for FET the pacing uses grade10, grade11, grade12 objects each with term1-term4 and totalLessons. Note that Mathematical Literacy is a fundamentally different subject from pure Mathematics: it focuses on using mathematics to understand and solve real-life problems in authentic contexts (financial documents, bank statements, plans, newspaper articles, real data), not on abstract mathematical theory. (3) assessment -- informal (description + practices array) and formal (tasksPerYear=7, tasksPerTerm describes the programme: Grades 10 and 11 have Assignment+Test in Term 1, Assignment+Mid-year Exam in Term 2, Investigation+Test in Term 3, End-of-year Exam in Term 4; Grade 12 has Investigation+Test in Term 1, Assignment+Mid-year Exam in Term 2, Test+Trial Exam in Term 3, End-of-year Exam in Term 4). The programme array covers: Assignment (well-structured task, familiar contexts, 10% of SBA per assignment), Test (controlled conditions, 15-20% of SBA per test), Investigation (guided discovery, develops high-order thinking for Paper 2, 10% of SBA), Mid-year Examination (two papers: Paper 1 Basic Skills + Paper 2 Applications, 25-30% of SBA), Trial Examination for Grade 12 (25% of SBA, same structure as final NSC, Term 3), End-of-year Examination (75% of final promotion mark, two papers: Paper 1 Basic Skills and Paper 2 Applications, external for Grade 12, internal for Grades 10 and 11). Recording and Reporting: 7 levels of competence (Level 7: 80-100% Outstanding, Level 6: 70-79% Meritorious, Level 5: 60-69% Substantial, Level 4: 50-59% Adequate, Level 3: 40-49% Moderate, Level 2: 30-39% Elementary, Level 1: 0-29% Not achieved). Moderation: school-level, district, provincial; Grade 12 SBA externally moderated, Grade 12 exam externally set/marked/moderated; Grades 10 and 11 all internal. For the end-of-year Paper 1 (Basic Skills): taxonomy levels -- Level 1 (Knowing) 60% +/- 5%, Level 2 (Applying routine procedures in familiar contexts) 35% +/- 5%, Level 3 (Applying multi-step procedures in a variety of contexts) 5% minimum, Level 4 (Reasoning and reflecting) 0%. For the end-of-year Paper 2 (Applications): Level 1 (Knowing) 30% +/- 5%, Level 2 (Applying routine procedures in familiar contexts) 25% +/- 5%, Level 3 (Applying multi-step procedures in a variety of contexts) 35% +/- 5%, Level 4 (Reasoning and reflecting) 40% +/- 5%. Mathematical Literacy is NOT pure mathematics -- it focuses on real-world quantitative reasoning, interpreting authentic resources (newspaper articles, bank statements, plans), and applying mathematics in context. Assessment items and examinations draw on realistic and authentic contexts, not contrived problems with only a semblance of reality.
